facts.site: Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility
facts.title: danger tagging failure on ML-3202

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was no injury or loss. The potential outcome was rated 1 against the site's consequence scale, above the 0 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control ENERGY_SOURCE_IDENTIFICATION: the identification of every energy source for the task was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control ISOLATION_HANDBACK_CONTROL: the controlled removal of isolation and return to service had been bypassed, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.
Control PARK_UP_AND_RESTRAINT: the parking, chocking and restraint of equipment had been bypassed, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.
Control ZERO_ENERGY_VERIFICATION: the proving zero energy before intrusive work was not in place, and the accident investigation classified this as an absent or failed defence.

recommendations: Restore the identification of every energy source for the task on ML-3202 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
Restore the parking, chocking and restraint of equipment on ML-3202 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
Restore the proving zero energy before intrusive work on ML-3202 and record the spot check before this task is next authorised.
response.sequence: Work was under way in applying and verifying an isolation, specifically dissipating trapped and residual energy. ML-3202 (grinding mills) is in service for two-line ball milling. The task proceeded during a planned shutdown while the identification of every energy source for the task was in place but did not perform. The electrical energy involved is held as HV switchgear, and the recorded presentation was shock, arc flash, unplanned energisation.
response.summary: On 7 June 2009 an incident occurred on ML-3202 at Marrindal Concentrator and Hydrocarbon Transfer Facility during a planned shutdown, releasing electrical energy held as HV switchgear.
